statement: Let L = len(edges). Call a set S ⊆ {0,...,L-1} of edge indices valid when both of the following hold: (A) for every two nodes x, y ∈ {1,...,n} there is a sequence x = w_0, w_1, ..., w_k = y such that each consecutive pair {w_{j-1}, w_j} equals {u_i, v_i} for some index i ∈ S with t_i ∈ {1,3}; (B) the same condition with t_i ∈ {2,3} in place of {1,3}. If at least one valid S exists, the function returns r = L - m where m = min{|S| : S is valid}; otherwise it returns r = -1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, 0 <= r <= len(edges).
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: Call S ⊆ {0,...,len(edges)-1} valid when the type-{1,3} edges of S connect all of {1,...,n} and the type-{2,3} edges of S connect all of {1,...,n}. The function returns -1 if and only if no valid S exists, equivalently if and only if the graph on {1,...,n} with edge set {{u_i, v_i} : t_i ∈ {1,3}} is disconnected or the graph on {1,...,n} with edge set {{u_i, v_i} : t_i ∈ {2,3}} is disconnected.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r != -1, there exists a set S ⊆ {0,...,len(edges)-1} with |S| = len(edges) - r such that the type-{1,3} edges of S connect all of {1,...,n} and the type-{2,3} edges of S connect all of {1,...,n}.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r != -1, for every S ⊆ {0,...,len(edges)-1} such that the type-{1,3} edges of S connect all of {1,...,n} and the type-{2,3} edges of S connect all of {1,...,n}, it holds that |S| >= len(edges) - r.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r != -1, r <= len(edges) - (n - 1).
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: Let edges' be defined by edges'[i] = [t'_i, u_i, v_i] where t'_i = 2 if t_i = 1, t'_i = 1 if t_i = 2, and t'_i = 3 if t_i = 3. Then max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges') = max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges), with both equal to -1 in the infeasible case.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: For any bijection σ from {1,...,n} onto {1,...,n}, define edges'[i] = [t_i, min(σ(u_i), σ(v_i)), max(σ(u_i), σ(v_i))] for each i. Then max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges') = max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges), including the case where both are -1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: For any bijection π of {0,...,len(edges)-1}, define edges' by edges'[i] = edges[π(i)]. Then max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges') = max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges), including the case where both are -1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges) = r with r != -1, then max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges') = r' satisfies r' != -1 and r' >= r + 1. When max_num_edges_to_remove(n, edges) = -1, no constraint is asserted.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) < min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct; fix a triple (t, u, v) with 1 <= t <= 3 and 1 <= u < v <= n that is not equal to any (t_i, u_i, v_i), and let edges' be edges with [t, u, v] appended (so len(edges') = len(edges) + 1).

statement: If the graph on {1,...,n} with edge set {{u_i, v_i} : 0 <= i < len(edges)} is connected, the function returns r = len(edges) - (n - 1); otherwise it returns r = -1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct; every edge has t_i = 3.

statement: Let C1 be the graph on {1,...,n} with edge set {{u_i, v_i} : t_i = 1}, and spec_15 the graph on {1,...,n} with edge set {{u_i, v_i} : t_i = 2}. If both C1 and spec_15 are connected, the function returns r = len(edges) - 2*(n - 1); otherwise it returns r = -1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct; no edge has t_i = 3.

statement: Whenever the function returns r with r != -1, r >= len(edges) - 2*(n-1).
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.

statement: Call S ⊆ {0,...,len(edges)-1} valid when the type-{1,3} edges of S connect all of {1,...,n} and the type-{2,3} edges of S connect all of {1,...,n}. Whenever the function returns r with r != -1, every valid S with |S| = len(edges) - r satisfies |{i in S : t_i in {1,3}}| = n-1 and |{i in S : t_i in {2,3}}| = n-1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^5; 1 <= len(edges) <= min(10^5, 3*n*(n-1)/2); every edges[i] is a vector [t_i, u_i, v_i] of length 3 with 1 <= t_i <= 3 and 1 <= u_i < v_i <= n; all triples (t_i, u_i, v_i) are pairwise distinct.
